content:
This library is a hands-on tour. Open the linked examples instead of reading
the list as documentation.

## Library and Markdown

The [welcome note](/note/notes/welcome) demonstrates headings, tables, code, task
lists, aliases, tags, and links. [Design principles](/note/notes/design_principles)
has repeated incoming links, so its sidebar is a good backlinks example.

## Search and connections

Search for **serendipity**, **consent**, or **quiet corner**. Each term appears
across several sections. Then open [Graph field guide](/note/wiki/graph_field_guide)
and switch between relation and “known from” grouping.

## Structured records

- People: [Alex](/note/people/alex_morgan), [Amara](/note/people/amara_okafor), and the full People section
- Projects: [active](/note/projects/neighborhood_atlas/neighborhood_atlas), [planned](/note/projects/mobile_story_booth/mobile_story_booth), [completed](/note/projects/listening_garden/listening_garden), and [idea](/note/projects/night_market_signage/night_market_signage)
- Tasks: todo, in progress, blocked, and done records with subtasks and deadlines
- Calendar: social and work events, a weekly series, project links, and a cross-midnight event

## Other workspaces

Open **Canvas** for a visual project map. The Playlists section demonstrates
embedded video discovery, while Shortcuts shows internal and external
destinations grouped into tabs.

Return to [Welcome to the Neighborhood Atlas](/note/notes/welcome) whenever you want
a fresh trail through the graph.
